clue.text: Seek opinion from son on work of art

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing on another follows it, so the son comes after the artwork

parts.note: a painting is often called a canvas
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A painter asks their son what he thinks of a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work of art' looks like the thing being judged, but a canvas is also the painting itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To canvass is to go round asking people for their views or votes.

clue.text: Start of sentence for most serious kind of crime

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the upper-case letter a sentence begins with

definitions.note: adjective, as in a capital crime
definitions.meaning: second meaning: of an offence punishable by death

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' suggests a prison term, but it is the grammatical sentence that opens with an upper-case letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A capital letter starts a sentence, and a capital crime is one carrying the death penalty.

clue.text: Book group that includes 1984

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the fourth book of the Old Testament
second meaning: integers, of which 1984 is one

explanation.walkthrough: 1984 suggests Orwell's novel and a book club, but it is just a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers is a book of the Bible, and the set of numbers contains 1984.

clue.text: Keep being annoying, topless in low joint

indicators.note: without its top, a down answer loses its opening letter

parts.note: to rankle is to cause lasting irritation

explanation.surface: Someone keeps causing irritation, half-naked in a seedy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low joint' reads like a disreputable bar; it is the joint low down on the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint between foot and leg, the lowest major joint in the body.

clue.text: Depressing experience after star's last drink of the day?

indicators.note: after places the gloomy experience second, behind the star

parts.note: the Sun is our star
a downer is something that dispirits

explanation.surface: After a celebrity's last drink of the night, a gloomy hangover follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star's last' looks like a final letter selection, but the possessive just attaches the star to the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is an alcoholic drink taken at sunset, the end of the day.

clue.text: Recording some fellers' work

definitions.meaning: first meaning: writing something down in a log or record
second meaning: the trade of cutting down trees

explanation.surface: Writing down what some men do for a living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellers' reads as 'fellows', but it means people who fell trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Logging is both entering data in a log and the industry of felling timber.

clue.text: Ill-gotten gains as enticement drawing Conservative in

indicators.note: drawing something in pulls it inside, so the bait takes in a letter

parts.note: a lure entices
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Dirty money used as bait to win over a Tory politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing ... in' brackets the Conservative, so the bait goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre, as in 'filthy lucre', is money gained dishonourably.

clue.text: Information about senior staff in plant

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the next

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
senior means old
a staff is a rod or stick

explanation.surface: Office gossip about the senior staff is circulating in the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Senior staff' reads as management, but the two words are clued separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldenrod is a flowering plant with tall spikes of yellow blooms.

clue.text: First thing Milton and Swift have in common

definitions.meaning: first meaning: coming at the start

definitions.text: thing Milton and Swift have in common
definitions.meaning: second meaning: John Milton and Jonathan Swift both begin with J

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a question about literary style, but the shared thing is the letter J their first names start with.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means first in order, and an initial is the first letter of a name.

clue.text: At length, interrupting Earl and PM in a major way

indicators.note: something interrupting breaks into the middle of another thing

parts.note: Earl Grey was Prime Minister in the 1830s
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: Someone talking at length, interrupting a nobleman and the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At length' looks like a single phrase meaning lengthily, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatly means to a great degree, in a major way.

clue.text: Fruit turned up by politician with family

indicators.note: something turned is facing the other way, so the next word is read backwards

parts.note: the little word itself, to be turned round
a Member of Parliament
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A politician and his family dig up some fruit in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads as appeared, but it is the word up turned backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pumpkin is a large orange gourd, botanically a fruit.

clue.text: Clash produced by lines I encrypted?

indicators.note: en-crypted can be read as placed within a cipher, so the preceding letters go inside

parts.note: the word also supplies the cipher that wraps round the other letters
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural
taken as written

explanation.surface: A conflict arising because some text was put into cipher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Encrypted' does double duty, read as 'in code': it supplies the outer word and tells you to put the lines and I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To collide is to crash together, to clash physically.

clue.text: Consequently inscribed in tablet here, for ever

indicators.note: something inscribed in a surface is written within it, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: runs from the end of tablet through to the start of ever

explanation.surface: An epitaph carved on a stone tablet, here to stay for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore and consequently are synonyms, both meaning as a result.

clue.text: Live show's beginning, actor's going outside

indicators.note: going outside means wrapping round, so the exit surrounds the other letter

parts.note: an actor's departure from the stage is an exit

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of show

explanation.surface: As a live show starts, an actor heads out of the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' sounds like the adjective for a show, but it is the verb, meaning to be alive.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be alive, to have being.

clue.text: Member of defeated team — not keeper, proverbially

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone on the side that lost
second meaning: from the saying 'finders keepers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeper' looks like a goalkeeper in the team, but it comes from the playground saying 'finders keepers, losers weepers'.
explanation.definitionFit: In that saying the one who mislays something does not get to keep it, and on the field a loser is someone beaten.

clue.text: Step out here after row, being offensive about one part of speech

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the offensive word goes round the rest

parts.note: rank means foul or offensive
Roman numeral one
a verb is a grammatical word class

explanation.surface: After an argument you storm out, saying something rude about grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel, but it means rowing a boat; after it you step out onto the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: After a row on a river, the place you step ashore is the riverbank.

clue.text: Dotty aunt leading protest meeting, of course

indicators.note: dotty means crazy or scatterbrained, so these letters are muddled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
a rally is a mass gathering, often for a protest

explanation.surface: An eccentric aunt heads a demonstration, as you'd expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturally and of course are synonyms, both meaning as might be expected.

clue.text: Runs in shoddy stuff clubs, perhaps, provided as sportswear

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the next word

parts.note: tack is cheap, tasteless material
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
clubs is one of the four card suits

explanation.surface: Poor-quality gear from sports clubs, used as kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tracksuit is a loose two-piece outfit worn for training and sport.

clue.text: Cape always covered with plastic, or the other way around

indicators.note: something covered has another thing laid all round it, so the outer word wraps the first letters

parts.note: plastic is slang for credit cards, and Visa is a card brand
C is the abbreviation for cape on maps
ever means always

explanation.surface: A cape always wrapped in plastic sheeting, or the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' looks like the material, but it means a credit card.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice versa is the Latin-derived phrase for with the order reversed.

clue.text: Half a dozen tricks — they should be kept out of program

definitions.text: they should be kept out of program

parts.note: Roman numeral six
ruses are tricks

explanation.surface: Six tricks that ought to be dropped from a show's running order.
explanation.walkthrough: The spelling 'program' signals computing rather than a theatre programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Computer viruses are malicious code that security software tries to keep out of programs.

clue.text: Arranger of exhibition and artist appearing in court when disorderly

indicators.note: appearing in somewhere means being found inside it
disorderly means out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A gallery organiser and a painter end up in the dock after rowdy behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator selects and organises the items in a museum or gallery show.

clue.text: Party is breaking old record, moving to the left

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it
in an across answer moving leftwards means reading backwards

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a compact disc
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political party breaks an old record by shifting leftwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Old and record together are turned round, then IS breaks into them.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a party with dancing to recorded music.

clue.text: Clip poodle, for example? Not much

parts.note: to snip is to clip with scissors
a poodle is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: Trim a poodle? Hardly at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Clipping a poodle fits the surface, but clip and poodle are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A snippet is a small piece or scrap, so not much of something.

clue.text: E.g. part of vein exposed, cut, or damaged in operation

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the next word

parts.note: op is short for operation

indicators.note: damaged things are broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A surgical mishap: a vein laid open, cut or damaged during surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The vein is a seam of mineral in rock, not a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is rock, such as a mineral vein, that shows above the surface.

clue.text: More unusual notes separately stored by educational foundation?

indicators.note: things stored by something are kept inside it
separately means each one goes into its own gap rather than together

parts.note: the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are the basics of education
two musical notes, A and E

explanation.surface: Rare musical notes are kept apart in the archive of some school trust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separately' tells you each note goes into a different gap in the three Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarer is the comparative of rare, meaning less common.

clue.text: Create female apparel that's rough and ready

parts.note: to make is to create
a shift is a simple loose dress

explanation.surface: Run up a woman's dress that is crudely finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Something makeshift is improvised and serves temporarily, rough and ready.

clue.text: Sportsperson who runs part of league

definitions.text: Sportsperson who runs part of league

parts.words: Sportsperson who runs part of league
parts.note: surface reading: a player who manages part of a sports league
setter's reading: an old league is three statute units of distance, so a middle-distance athlete covers a third of one

explanation.walkthrough: League suggests a football competition; it is also an old measure of about three miles.
explanation.definitionFit: A middle-distance runner specialising in the mile race covers a third of a league.

clue.text: Contemptuously reject what's new after incitement

indicators.note: after places the new thing second, behind the incitement

parts.note: a spur is a stimulus or incitement
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Dismissing the latest thing after being provoked.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn is to reject with disdain.

clue.text: Went on voyage, i.e. with salts at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of the abbreviation
salts are old sailors, taken here for their letters

explanation.surface: A sailor's log: we departed, that is, with the old salts out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: To set sail is to begin a sea journey.

clue.text: Unscrupulous financial operator seizing power, one who takes over

indicators.note: seizing something means grabbing hold of it, so the outer word holds a letter inside

parts.note: a usurer lends money at extortionate interest
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A crooked moneylender grabs control and takes over the business.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurper wrongfully seizes a throne or position held by another.

clue.text: Batsman who's out?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, the batsman facing the bowling is the one on strike
second meaning: a worker who has walked out in an industrial dispute

explanation.walkthrough: A batsman who is out is dismissed, but here 'out' means on strike from work; in cricket the batsman receiving the ball is also so called.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the cricketer facing the bowler and an employee withdrawing labour.

clue.text: Upper garment worn by male or female in turret?

definitions.text: Upper garment worn by male or female
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sleeveless knitted pullover
second meaning: the revolving part on top of an armoured vehicle

explanation.surface: A unisex sweater worn up in a castle tower.
explanation.walkthrough: A turret reads as part of a castle, but it is also what sits on top of a military tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A tank top is a sleeveless jumper, and literally a tank's top is its turret.
